articles.headline: Liverpool loanee Harvey Elliott sent off for two yellows inside a minute
articles.description: Liverpool loanee Harvey Elliott was sent off for two yellow card in under a minute during Valencia's 2-1 defeat to Villareal in LaLiga on Saturday.
articles.headlineJa: リヴァプールのローン中のハーヴェイ・エリオット、1分間に2枚のイエローカードで退場
articles.descriptionJa: 土曜日のラ・リーガ、バレンシアがビジャレアルに1-2で敗れた試合において、リヴァプールから期限付き移籍中のハーヴェイ・エリオットが、1分足らずの間に2枚のイエローカードを受けて退場処分となった。
articles.body:
Liverpool loanee Harvey Elliott was sent off for two yellow card in under a minute during Valencia's 2-1 defeat to Villarreal in LaLiga on Saturday. 

It took Elliott's loan spell in Spain thus far from bad to worse with the 23-year-old yet to start for Valencia, making six substitute appearances this season. He is also yet to score or assist for the LaLiga side.  

The game was level at 1-1 at the time of his sending off, the 89th minute, with Villareal going on to take all three points in the sixth minute of stoppage time as Georges Mikautadze put one past the 10-man Valencia side. 

Elliott appeared frustrated with a decision going against one of his teammates, before referee Alejandro Quintero Gonzalez booked him twice in the space of seconds for apparent dissent. 

Speaking after the game, Valencia boss Javier Aguirre seemingly took responsibility for the red card himself, while admitting it was an "irritating" decision.

"With 11 of us against their 10, we weren't doing badly," he said.

"We were in the game. And then, an absurd, ridiculous sending-off, obviously for talking. He barely speaks Spanish, so I don't know what he could have said to the referee, or perhaps the referee is bilingual, I really don't know. But it was for talking and that really irritates me, yes, yes.

"I've already made that clear to him, and there are rules, and we can't ... It's not his fault, it's my fault, if anything, for picking the players I do and playing the way we do. It's entirely my fault, but I'll sort it out internally and say what I need to say."

Elliott left Liverpool on loan in the summer after failing to force his way into new manager Andoni Iraola's plans. The move followed a horror spell on loan at Aston Villa last season, where he was frozen out of the first-team squad by Unai Emery.

articles.headline: NFL, NFLPA handling joint review of Jalen Hurts' blood clot diagnosis
articles.description: The NFL and NFL Players Association are working together to review the handling of Jalen Hurts' blood clot diagnosis.
articles.headlineJa: NFLとNFLPA、ジェイレン・ハーツの血栓診断への対応について共同調査を実施
articles.descriptionJa: NFLとNFL選手会（NFLPA）は、ジェイレン・ハーツの血栓診断に関する対応を検証するため、共同で調査を進めている。
articles.body:
The NFL and NFL Players Association are working together to review the handling of Jalen Hurts' blood clot diagnosis.

The league and players' union released a joint statement Sunday saying they are looking into it after the NFLPA called for an investigation earlier in the week.

Hurts was placed on injured reserve and is expected to miss the rest of the season after a blood clot in his left calf traveled to his lungs. The Philadelphia Eagles and agent Nicole Lynn said Monday that Hurts has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli.

His treatment involves blood thinners, and Hurts will not be allowed to participate in any football activities until he is off them.

NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said Wednesday that the league welcomed an investigation after Dr. Allen Sills, the league's chief medical officer, gave a passionate defense of the Eagles' medical staff.

The Eagles previously said Hurts was injured when he took a cleat to his calf area Oct. 4 in a game against the Los Angeles Rams.

Hurts informed the medical staff of the injury after practice Oct. 8. The Super Bowl LIX MVP was back at practice the next day before the team left for London to play the Jacksonville Jaguars. Hurts was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis but played against Jacksonville on Oct. 11.

"Obviously, there was a medical evaluation, and I think our protocols were incredibly good there," Goodell said Wednesday. "The protocols were followed. Our process is to make sure that's the case, and our chief medical officer has gone through that, so we're comfortable that what we've seen in the protocols have happened."

articles.headline: Man City must be 'more clinical,' Enzo Maresca demands
articles.description: Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca says his side needs to be more clinical and "score more goals" after they were beaten by Aston Villa on Saturday.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・シティは「もっと決定力が必要」、エンツォ・マレスカ監督が要求
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティのエンツォ・マレスカ監督は、土曜日のアストン・ヴィラ戦に敗れた後、チームはもっと決定力を高め、「より多くのゴールを決める」必要があると語った。
articles.body:
Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca says his side needs to be more clinical and "score more goals" after they were beaten by Aston Villa on Saturday.

City registered 15 shots during their defeat but only managed to score once courtesy of Erling Haaland's second-half header.

Villa keeper Zion Suzuki was in inspired form as he made six saves, while City twice hit the post through Iliman Ndiaye and Josko Gvardiol in a frustrating afternoon at Villa Park.

City are the second highest scorers in the league but Maresca still thinks his team need to be more clinical.

He said: "Now I need to review the game.

"For sure if you see the amount of time we spent in their box, sometimes we need to be more accurate and precise in the final third and score more goals.

"We spent most of the game in their side, in their box in the final third.

"Sometimes you have to be more clinical when you have chances but also more precise on the last pass, we have to learn from that.

"You can always do something better but for me when you plan a game, especially against this team, you know you are going to concede some transitions because they wait for that."

Rayan Cherki was left on the bench in last week's win over Ipswich and also endured a frustrating afternoon against Villa after he was booked in the 38th minute.

The 23-year-old, who has scored six times this season, was taken off at half time on Saturday as well as in the defeat to PSG in the Champions League last week but Maresca says his substitution was down to him being on a yellow.

He added: "The last game I changed him at half time, him and Rúben Dias against PSG. It's not just Rayan.

"It's just in that moment where we can improve things and change things. Him and Rayan were both on yellow card and sometimes the referee with the noise can judge in different ways."

City lost their three-point lead at the top of the table after Arsenal earned a 2-0 victory over Everton but still remain at the summit.

Captain Dias is aiming for his side to produce the perfect reaction against Brighton in the Carabao Cup this week.

- Man City lose 100% Premier League record with defeat at Aston Villa

- Marc Guéhi form doesn't worry Man City boss Enzo Maresca despite errors

He told City's website: "We had chances and they ended up scoring two goals in two transitions -- very efficient. Room to improve, we need to do better.

"I felt like we were dangerous on many occasions, even if the finish wasn't there we arrived in dangerous places but not able to play. A word of appreciation to the boys because we kept fighting to the end.

"It is what it is. Whatever happens we need to react to it. The team had a very good reaction. The second one was tough because it was very close to our equaliser. We kept going and tried to create chances. Not our day but we keep moving forward."

articles.headline: Arsenal unlocked key to set-piece dominance - Mikel Arteta
articles.description: Mikel Arteta is confident Arsenal will rediscover their potency from set-pieces after breaking their duck in Saturday's 2-0 Premier League victory over Everton.
articles.headlineJa: アーセナルはセットプレー支配の鍵を解明 - ミケル・アルテタ
articles.descriptionJa: ミケル・アルテタは、土曜日のプレミアリーグ、エヴァートン戦での2-0の勝利でセットプレーからの得点を挙げたことで、アーセナルが再びその威力を発揮できるようになると確信している。
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta is confident Arsenal will rediscover their potency from set-pieces after breaking their duck in Saturday's 2-0 Premier League victory over Everton.

The Gunners developed a reputation as set-piece specialists last term, scoring 29 times from corners, free-kicks and penalties en route to winning the title.

Yet Ezri Konsa's scrambled, seventh-minute opener against the Toffees marked the first time the reigning champions had scored from a set play in eight top-flight games this campaign.

"I'm sure that's going to unlock something and that belief of the players," manager Arteta said. "So they are really convinced.

"You have to see them when we train the level of attention and how much they believe in what we do and what Nico [Jover, set-piece coach] does as well.

"There's no question about that, but at the end he has to come through and he has to make the difference and we know that that is a massive welcome for us."

Gabriel's second-half header from a Ben White cross sealed Arsenal's seventh win in eight league games.

Konsa's first goal for the club, following a Martin Odegaard corner, set the Gunners on course to move level on 21 points with leaders Manchester City, on the back of a 2-2 Champions League draw away to Bayern Munich.

"We hadn't scored from a set-piece, which we were disappointed with because we had generated so many chances as well," Arteta said.

"I think in midweek we should have scored at least two in Munich and we didn't and that would probably win us the game.

"We know that in every phase of play we want to be the best and we're not going to stop until we do it."

- Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal, Man United, Liverpool track Bayern star Karl

- Arsenal's Mikel Arteta collecting evidence on rival managers after yellow card

- Make way for Arsenal, the people's Premier League champions

Arsenal sit second on goal difference after table-topping City suffered their first defeat of the season, losing 2-1 at Aston Villa in Saturday's lunchtime kick-off.

"We have to just focus on what we can do and we are very pleased with 90 per cent of the results and performances that we have apart from the Brighton game," Arteta said, whose side lost 3-0 at the Amex Stadium last month.

Arsenal's hectic fixture list continues with Tuesday evening's Carabao Cup fourth-round tie away to League Two Fleetwood before they travel to Liverpool in the league next Sunday.

Arteta was delighted to end a challenging week, which began with last Sunday's 1-0 success at Nottingham Forest before the midweek visit to Munich, with two wins and a draw.

"Yes, we're very happy with the [Everton] victory, with the performance and with the week, because we were given a terrible schedule," the Spaniard said.

"We have overcome every hurdle, on top of some injuries, and I love the mentality of the team and the quality that we've shown."

articles.headline: Bruno Fernandes left out by Man United after Michael Carrick criticism
articles.description: Bruno Fernandes has been left out of the Manchester United team to face Bournemouth after his public criticism of head coach Michael Carrick.
articles.body:
Bruno Fernandes has been left out of the Manchester United team to face Bournemouth after his public criticism of head coach Michael Carrick.

The Portuguese midfielder was named on the bench for the visit of Marco Rose's side to Old Trafford on Sunday. Harry Maguire was named captain in his absence.

Fernandes was critical of Carrick's tactical approach during the 4-1 defeat to Como on Wednesday.

He hinted he was disappointed with instructions to not press Como. When the comments were put to Carrick, he hit back by saying: "If you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren't going to win."

Carrick told Sky Sports after naming Fernandes on the bench that his team selection was "pure football."

He added: "It's always a difficult decision. We have to make what we feel is the right one for the team to get the performance that we want."

Carrick confirmed Lisandro Martínez wasn't fit enough to start.

Asked at a news conference on Friday whether he would consider dropping Fernandes against Bournemouth, Carrick refused to answer and said only that he would "do what's best for the football club."

Martínez escaped a similar punishment after his public criticism of director of football Jason Wilcox and the board.

Martínez issued an apology, received a fine but started the next game against Leeds United before going off at halftime with an injury.

articles.headline: Sources: Peyton Manning not expected to be candidate for Colts' vacant GM job
articles.description: The Colts have not approached Peyton Manning about their vacant GM job nor would the ex-QB be expected to be interested in the position, according to sources.
articles.body:
Peyton Manning has many jobs -- Omaha Productions, the "ManningCast," commercial pitchman -- but he is not expected to add Indianapolis Colts general manager to his list of titles and responsibilities, league sources told ESPN.

The Colts have not approached Manning about their vacant GM job nor would the Hall of Fame quarterback be expected to be interested in the position, sources said. Manning has not trained or aspired to become an NFL general manager, not with all that he has going on in his life.

Manning has created a post-football, off-the-field career as successful as the one he had on the gridiron. He has two children in high school, "Monday Night Football" obligations and commercial shoots scattered across his calendar.

The timing to become an NFL general manager, which requires day-to-day attention, would not be right, according to sources.

The Colts fired Chris Ballard on Monday, ending his run of nine-plus seasons as their GM. Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon said in a statement that the Colts planned to conduct "a thorough search" for their next GM, adding that the franchise would "take the time necessary to identify the right leader for the future of this organization."

Manning would be willing to listen and consider any NFL opportunities at any time, but the Colts have not discussed any of those possibilities with him, according to sources. It's possible that some could come in the future, sources said, but those discussions likely would involve higher-profile positions similar to the ones that other former NFL quarterbacks have accepted with other franchises.

Former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Tom Brady has become a limited owner with the Las Vegas Raiders as well as a sounding board for the organization. Former Atlanta Falcons quarterback Matt Ryan has returned to the franchise as its president of football. And former Jacksonville Jaguars standout offensive tackle Tony Boselli is the team's executive vice president of football operations.

In 2024, Manning publicly said that running an NFL franchise was not on his radar at that time. He said he was enjoying working on the "ManningCast" with his brother, Eli, and being at home with his family.

By having the "ManningCast" and Omaha Productions, Manning has been able to stay close to the sport and have as much work as he wants without the demands of running a team.

The Colts could hold sentimental appeal to Manning, just as the Denver Broncos once did for John Elway and the Miami Dolphins did for Dan Marino. Elway became the Broncos' general manager, and Marino has been a special adviser for the Dolphins since August 2014.

Ballard, in the final year of his contract, was in a make-or-break season after Indianapolis' seven-game losing streak in 2025 derailed its 8-2 start and prompted Irsay-Gordon and her sisters to consider widespread changes. The Colts were the first team to ever reach six games over .500 and finish with a losing record.

It might look odd to see the lowest-ranked fantasy passers ahead of typical RB2 and WR2 options, but the potential scoring impact demands it.

If your league is a standard flex, note that rankings without QBs appear below the superflex rankings. However you prefer to play, good luck this week!

articles.headline: Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois out of Clasico with flu
articles.description: Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois will miss the team's Clásico clash with Barcelona with flu, the club said on Sunday.
articles.body:
Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois will miss the team's Clásico clash with Barcelona with flu, the club said on Sunday.

Courtois, 34, is a key player for Madrid, but is now set to be absent for the LaLiga match at Camp Nou, which kicks off with Madrid trailing leaders Barça by six points in the table.

He would be replaced in goal by Andriy Lunin, 27, who has been a regular deputy for Courtois in recent seasons, including in Madrid's run to the Champions League final in 2024.

"Courtois is a last-minute withdrawal from tonight's LaLiga matchday 10 game between Real Madrid and Barcelona due to a bout of the flu," the club said in a brief statement. "Illia Voloshyn has been called up to the squad in his place."

However a source also told ESPN that while the squad were already in Barcelona, Madrid were not completely ruling out Courtois travelling to join them later in the day, in time for the game, if his condition were to improve significantly.

Madrid go into the Clásico under pressure, having already lost twice in LaLiga this season -- at Real Betis and Atletico Madrid -- while Barcelona have won all of their league games.

However, Madrid's form has improved since the international break, with Courtois playing a starring role, including in their 4-1 Champions League win over RB Leipzig in midweek.

The visitors will also be without Vinícius Júnior at Camp Nou, as he continues his four-game domestic ban.

Additional reporting from ESPN's Rodra.

Bayern Munich forward Lennart Karl is being tracked by Arsenal, Manchester United and Liverpool, while United defender Leny Yoro is on the radar of AC Milan. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Arsenal, Manchester United and Liverpool are monitoring Bayern Munich forward Lennart Karl, following concerns over his game time, according to TEAMtalk. Despite signing a new long-term deal earlier this year, the 18-year-old Germany international has made nine appearances this season -- scoring once and adding an assist -- and could consider an exit if his role does not expand.

- Manchester United defender Leny Yoro is on the radar of AC Milan ahead of the summer, says Calciomercato. Yoro, 20, has struggled since moving from Lille for €62 million in 2024, but former United boss Ruben Amorim is keen to bring him to San Siro to add depth to his defense. A fee of around €50 million is expected to be enough for the France international to move on.

- Trent Alexander-Arnold is not currently considered a concrete target for Liverpool as they evaluate future right-back options, reports Football Insider. Although the 28-year-old has experienced limited minutes at Real Madrid due to competition from Denzel Dumfries and Federico Valverde, there is no active movement toward an Anfield return.

- Tottenham Hotspur and Newcastle United have made inquiries regarding AC Milan duo Fikayo Tomori and Ruben Loftus-Cheek ahead of January, TEAMtalk reports. The Rossoneri are open to letting both players leave, with 28-year-old defender Tomori featuring just three times under Ruben Amorim and 30-year-old midfielder Loftus-Cheek making eight appearances across all competitions.

articles.descriptionJa: デトロイト・ピストンズ（2勝0敗、東カンファレンス2位）対フィラデルフィア・76ers（3勝0敗、東カンファレンス1位）
articles.body:
Detroit Pistons (2-0, second in the Eastern Conference) vs. Philadelphia 76ers (3-0, first in the Eastern Conference)


              Philadelphia; Sunday, 7:30 p.m. EDT


              LINE: 76ers -2.5; over/under is 226.5


              BOTTOM LINE: Philadelphia will try to build upon its three-game win streak with a victory over Detroit.


              Philadelphia went 45-37 overall and 27-25 in Eastern Conference action a season ago. The 76ers gave up 116.1 points per game while committing 20.3 fouls last season.


              Detroit went 60-22 overall and 39-13 in Eastern Conference action during the 2025-26 season. The Pistons averaged 10.4 steals, 6.4 blocks and 14.2 turnovers per game last season.


              INJURIES: 76ers: Ariel Hukporti: out for season (achilles), Tacko Fall: out (hip), Dominick Barlow: out (back), LeBron James: out (back).


              Pistons: Ausar Thompson: day to day (ankle), Jalen Duren: out (hamstring).


              ------

              Boston; Monday, 7:30 p.m. EDT

articles.headline: Miami faces Dallas, looks to end 3-game slide
articles.description: Dallas Mavericks (1-2, 12th in the Western Conference) vs. Miami Heat (0-3, 14th in the Eastern Conference)
articles.body:
Dallas Mavericks (1-2, 12th in the Western Conference) vs. Miami Heat (0-3, 14th in the Eastern Conference)


              Miami; Monday, 7:30 p.m. EDT


              BOTTOM LINE: Miami aims to end its three-game losing streak when the Heat play Dallas.


              Miami went 43-39 overall last season while going 26-15 at home. The Heat averaged 120.9 points per game last season, 54.7 in the paint, 19.6 off of turnovers and 18.4 on fast breaks.


              Dallas finished 26-56 overall a season ago while going 10-31 on the road. The Mavericks averaged 15.9 points off of turnovers, 13.6 second-chance points and 43.3 bench points last season.


              INJURIES: Heat: None listed.


              Mavericks: Kyrie Irving: out (knee), Cooper Flagg: out (shoulder), Tarik Biberovic: out (heel), Caleb Martin: out (thumb), Dereck Lively II: out (foot), Santi Aldama: out (knee).

articles.headline: Rockets face the Hawks on 3-game win streak
articles.description: Atlanta Hawks (2-1, fourth in the Eastern Conference) vs. Houston Rockets (3-0, first in the Western Conference)
articles.body:
Atlanta Hawks (2-1, fourth in the Eastern Conference) vs. Houston Rockets (3-0, first in the Western Conference)


              Houston; Monday, 8:30 p.m. EDT


              BOTTOM LINE: Houston is looking to keep its three-game win streak going when the Rockets take on Atlanta.


              Houston finished 52-30 overall a season ago while going 30-11 at home. The Rockets averaged 115.2 points per game last season, 53.0 in the paint, 17.1 off of turnovers and 14.0 on fast breaks.


              Atlanta went 46-36 overall, 27-25 in Eastern Conference action and 22-19 on the road a season ago. The Hawks shot 47.4% from the field and 37.1% from 3-point range last season.


              The teams meet for the second time this season. The Rockets won 121-114 in the last matchup on Oct. 25.


              INJURIES: Rockets: Marcus Smart: out (forearm), Fred VanVleet: out (rest), Steven Adams: out (rest).


              Hawks: Henri Veesaar: out for season (acl), Mouhamed Gueye: out (foot).

articles.headline: Charlotte and Washington square off in conference showdown
articles.description: Washington Wizards (1-1, sixth in the Eastern Conference) vs. Charlotte Hornets (2-1, fifth in the Eastern Conference)
articles.body:
Washington Wizards (1-1, sixth in the Eastern Conference) vs. Charlotte Hornets (2-1, fifth in the Eastern Conference)


              Charlotte, North Carolina; Monday, 7 p.m. EDT


              BOTTOM LINE: Eastern Conference foes Charlotte and Washington face off on Monday.


              Charlotte finished 44-38 overall, 11-5 in Southeast Division action and 21-20 at home last season. The Hornets averaged 116.0 points per game last season, 45.2 in the paint, 15.6 off of turnovers and 13.3 on fast breaks.


              Washington finished 17-65 overall and 11-41 in Eastern Conference games during the 2025-26 season. The Wizards allowed opponents to score 124.9 points per game and shoot 48.8% from the field last season.


              INJURIES: Hornets: Grant Williams: out (hamstring), Kylan Boswell: out (knee), Kon Knueppel: out (hamstring), Coby White: out (calf).


              Wizards: AJ Dybantsa: out (ankle), Tristan Vukcevic: out (hip), Jamir Watkins: out for season (acl).
